The report by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) examines grant programs awarded by the Departments of Health and Human Services (HHS), Labor (DOL), and Justice (DOJ) from 2007 to 2015 that were subject to statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring. The report identified 2,586 grantees who received funding through at least 53 grant programs, with HHS identifying one grant program, the Projects for Assistance in Transition from Homelessness (PATH), where nonprofits could be primary recipients but no faith-based organizations (FBOs) were awarded grants. DOL identified 19 potential FBOs among the grantees subject to statutory restrictions, while DOJ identified 11 faith-based grantees that certified they were exempt from the restrictions.

The report also found that DOL and HHS did not have records of FBOs requesting exemptions from the statutory restrictions. The agencies informed grant applicants of the restrictions through grant announcements and other means. Of the nine FBOs identified by the GAO that certified they were exempt, they reported that the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA) exemptions were important for their mission and hiring practices.

The report concludes by stating that the Departments of Labor, Justice, and Health and Human Services were provided with a draft of the report and technical comments were incorporated as appropriate. The report will be distributed to the Secretaries of Health and Human Services and Labor, the Attorney General, and appropriate congressional committees 30 days after the report date. It will also be available on the GAO website.
